evaluation; mixed-methods research; reproducible data science;

## Research Experience

::: cv-entry
[November 2025–Present]{.cv-date} [Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery
and Validation in Chemo-Immunotherapy]{.cv-entry-title} — Independent
Study, ***NSF REU Research Stipend,*** Binghamton University

[Faculty Mentors: Dr. Nancy Guo]{.cv-mentor}

- Contribute 10 hrs/week to chemo-immunotherapy biomarker discovery by
  reproducing RNA-seq and scRNA-seq preprocessing, clustering TCR
  expansion with K-means, and analyzing treatment-response signatures.
- Transform and validate single-cell RNA-seq data through quality
  control, normalization, gene filtering, and highly variable gene
  selection.
- Perform differential expression analysis, cross-study comparisons, and
  Gene Set Enrichment Analysis to identify and validate
  treatment-response biomarkers and biological pathways (manuscript in
  preparation).
:::

::: cv-entry
[August 2025–Present]{.cv-date} [Machine Learning for Health Information
Avoidance]{.cv-entry-title} — Independent Study, Binghamton University\
[Faculty Mentors: Dr. Heather Orom (University at Buffalo), Dr. Shane
McCarty and Dr.Kargin Vladislav]{.cv-mentor}

- Predict health information avoidance in colorectal cancer using
  logistic regression, multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS),
  and random forest classifiers in R with tidymodels and caret.
- Evaluate and compare model performance using cross-validation and
  predictive metrics, documenting results in a reproducible Quarto and
  LaTeX [report](https://zihanhei.quarto.pub/avoider-report/)
  (manuscript under review).
:::

::: cv-entry

- Contributed quantitative analyses to a mixed-methods study integrating

::: cv-entry
[June 2025–Present]{.cv-date} [Examining Zero-Sum Beliefs and Political

## Data Science Projects

::: cv-entry
[January 2026–Present]{.cv-date} [Histopathology Thyroid Cancer
Detection Using YOLO]{.cv-entry-title} — Group Project, Binghamton
University \| [Group
project](https://github.com/Zihan-Hei/Histopathology-Thyroid-Cancer-Detection-A-Triple-Class-YOLO26-Approach)

- Develop a YOLO26-based deep-learning workflow for thyroid cancer,
  abnormal, and normal histopathology tissue detection, including model
  training, evaluation, and error analysis.
- Evaluate model performance through Type I (false positive) and Type II
  (false negative) error analysis and interpret confusion matrices for
  class imbalance and dataset representativeness.
- Visualize and document model performance and limitations for potential
  pre-screening applications (manuscript in preparation).
:::

- Implemented deep reinforcement-learning agents in PyTorch to play
  Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect Four through self-play.
- Designed neural networks mapping board states to action values and
  visualized training performance using Matplotlib.
